title: 100 Airbnb Facts
description: A collection of historical, statistical, and fun facts about Airbnb.

airbnb_facts.fact: Airbnb was originally named 'AirBed & Breakfast'.
The idea was born in October 2007 when founders Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia couldn't afford their San Francisco rent.
A local design conference had sold out all hotels, prompting the founders to rent out three air mattresses on their living room floor.
The very first guests were provided with airbeds and a breakfast of Pop-Tarts.
The first guest ever on Airbnb was Amol Surve, a design student from India.
Nate Blecharczyk, a former roommate and software engineer, joined as the third co-founder in early 2008 to build the website.
The official Airbedandbreakfast.com website launched on August 11, 2008.
In its early days, the platform was used primarily to find lodging for high-profile events like the 2008 Democratic National Convention.
To fund the site initially, the founders created custom cereal boxes: 'Obama O’s' and 'Cap'n McCain's'.
They sold 800 boxes of the political cereal at $40 each, raising $30,000 for the company.
Paul Graham of Y Combinator famously accepted Airbnb into his incubator in 2009 because he was impressed they managed to sell cereal at $40 a box.
During Y Combinator, the founders flew to New York City to meet hosts and professionally photograph their spaces to increase bookings.
The name was officially shortened to 'Airbnb' in March 2009.
By April 2009, the company received its first major seed funding of $600,000 from Sequoia Capital.
In the early days, Brian Chesky lived entirely out of Airbnb listings for months to dogfood the product.
The first international booking took place in 2008 when a user from the US booked a stay in Canada.
Barry Manilow's drummer was one of the early success stories, renting out a whole house while on tour.
Airbnb's iconic logo, the 'Bélo', was introduced in 2014.
The Bélo is designed to symbolize four things: People, Places, Love, and Airbnb.
Airbnb's core mission and tagline is 'Belong Anywhere'.
Airbnb went public on December 10, 2020.
The company trades on the NASDAQ under the ticker symbol ABNB.
On its first day of trading, Airbnb's valuation surpassed $100 billion.
Airbnb does not actually own any of the real estate properties listed on its platform.
The platform makes money primarily by charging a service fee to both guests and hosts.
Airbnb has active listings in over 220 countries and regions.
There are Airbnb listings in more than 100,000 cities worldwide.
The platform boasts over 5 million hosts globally.
There are over 7 million active listings on Airbnb.
More than 1.5 billion guest arrivals have occurred through Airbnb since its founding.
On any given night, millions of people are sleeping in an Airbnb.
Airbnb is banned or heavily restricted in a few cities, such as New York City (under Local Law 18).
In 2022, Airbnb permanently suspended all operations in Russia and Belarus.
Airbnb previously operated in China under the brand name 'Aibiying' before closing its domestic business there in 2022.
Treehouses are historically one of the most wish-listed property types on Airbnb.
You can rent out entire private islands on the platform.
There are thousands of historical castles available for rent.
Airbnb features a dedicated 'OMG!' category for highly unusual homes, like UFOs and giant boots.
In 2022, Airbnb launched a $1 million 'OMG! Fund' to help creators build the craziest home ideas.
There are over 40,000 farms listed on Airbnb.
You can stay in an actual converted train car via the platform.
In 2023, Airbnb offered a stay at a real-life replica of Shrek's Swamp in Scotland.
To celebrate the Barbie movie, Ken hosted guests at the Barbie Malibu Dreamhouse.
The original 'Home Alone' house in Chicago was listed for a one-night stay.
In 2020, the last remaining Blockbuster video store in Bend, Oregon, was listed for 90s-themed sleepovers.
Guests once had the chance to sleep inside the glass pyramid of the Louvre Museum in Paris.
A custom-built underwater bedroom in the Aquarium de Paris was once listed, surrounded by sharks.
Bran Castle in Transylvania, the inspiration for Dracula's castle, hosted guests on Halloween in 2016.
The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air mansion was hosted by Will Smith for a limited time.
A floating house was once sailed down the River Thames in London to celebrate new UK regulations.
The 'Superhost' program was launched to recognize hosts who provide exceptional hospitality.
To be a Superhost, you must maintain a 4.8 or higher overall rating.
Superhosts must also have a cancellation rate of less than 1%.
In 2023, Airbnb introduced 'Guest Favorites', a collection of the 2 million most-loved homes on the platform.
AirCover for Hosts provides $3 million in damage protection and $1 million in liability insurance.
AirCover for Guests ensures if a host cancels within 30 days, Airbnb will find a similar or better home, or refund the guest.
Airbnb Plus was a tier of homes verified for quality and design in person.
Airbnb Luxe features ultra-luxury properties with dedicated trip designers.
In 2016, Airbnb launched 'Experiences', allowing locals to host tours, classes, and activities.
During the pandemic in 2020, Airbnb launched 'Online Experiences' over Zoom.
Airbnb.org is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit that facilitates temporary stays for people in crisis.
The idea for emergency housing started in 2012 when a host offered her home for free to people displaced by Hurricane Sandy.
Airbnb.org committed to providing temporary housing to 100,000 Ukrainian refugees in 2022.
The platform also provided housing for 20,000 Afghan refugees in 2021.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, hosts offered places to stay for frontline medical workers.
Airbnb operates a 'Frontline stays' program to support disaster relief workers.
The Open Homes program (now part of Airbnb.org) originally launched to help medical patients traveling for treatment.
Airbnb has pledged to operate as a net-zero company for corporate greenhouse gas emissions by 2030.
Airbnb established a Community Fund to distribute $100 million over 10 years to organizations supporting host communities.
The company actively partners with the NAACP to increase the number of Black hosts and guests on the platform.
Airbnb’s headquarters is located at 888 Brannan Street in San Francisco.
Many of the meeting rooms at Airbnb's headquarters are exact replicas of actual listings on the platform.
Airbnb is a dog-friendly workplace, with many employees bringing their dogs to the office.
Employees receive an annual travel stipend to stay in Airbnbs and experience the product firsthand.
In 2022, Brian Chesky announced a 'Live and Work Anywhere' policy, allowing employees to work remotely from anywhere in their home country without a pay cut.
Co-founders Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia both attended the Rhode Island School of Design (RISD).
Because of its design roots, design thinking is heavily embedded in Airbnb's product development.
Airbnb typically announces major platform updates twice a year, known as the Summer and Winter Releases.
In 2022, Brian Chesky resumed his early-days habit and began living in Airbnbs full-time to test the platform.
The company has an internal data university to teach employees how to make data-driven decisions.
In 2022, Airbnb completely overhauled its search function with 'Airbnb Categories', letting users search by style rather than just destination.
A feature called 'Split Stays' allows guests booking longer trips to automatically split their stay between two different homes.
'Instant Book' allows guests to book immediately without waiting for host approval.
Airbnb's 'Smart Pricing' uses machine learning to automatically adjust a host's prices based on local demand.
Airbnb has deployed sophisticated anti-party technology to identify high-risk bookings and prevent unauthorized parties.
The platform automatically translates reviews and listing descriptions into dozens of languages.
Airbnb introduced 'Pay Less Up Front' to let guests pay a deposit at booking and the remainder closer to the check-in date.
Airbnb’s Wishlists feature was so successful upon launch that it increased engagement by 30% almost instantly.
The platform has a dedicated Neighborhood Support line for neighbors to report disturbances at a listing.
In 2023, Airbnb revamped user profiles to create 'Host Passports', giving guests more context about who they are staying with.
The highest altitude Airbnb ever listed was a basecamp on Mount Everest.
The most booked Airbnb in the world is reportedly a small, mushroom-shaped dome cabin in Aptos, California.
New Year's Eve is traditionally one of the biggest booking nights of the year for Airbnb globally.
Women make up the majority of Airbnb’s global host community.
Seniors (hosts aged 60+) are consistently rated as the most hospitable demographic on the platform.
Airbnb bought the hotel booking app HotelTonight in 2019.
The first major city to pass comprehensive short-term rental laws regulating Airbnb was San Francisco.
During the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, roughly 20% of all attendees stayed in an Airbnb.
Airbnb has a dedicated trust and safety team that works 24/7 to support the community globally.
In 2023, Airbnb reintroduced 'Airbnb Rooms', getting back to its roots by highlighting private rooms and authentic host connections.
